newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Malbak may surprise on upside.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Malbak may surprise on upside.

text.p: South African conglomerate Malbak Ltd is expected to post year earnings up a subdued 10 percent amid mixed performances from the group's subsidiaries, analysts said on Friday.
But others said Malbak's earnings may surprise on the upside following stronger-than-expected results this month from listed subsidiaries South African Druggists, Foodcorp Ltd and Kohler Ltd.
"SA Druggist's results were better than we expected and I think people may have to revise up their forecasts," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Foodcorp's earnings were up 16.3 percent against analysts consensus forecast of 13 percent and SA Druggists earnings were up 12.5 percent against analysts 11.0 percent consensus rise. Kohler posted earnings up 20.2 percent against analysts consensus forecast of a 15 percent rise.
Unlisted subsidiaries were seen producing a mixed bag of results with Tedelex having had a bad year, but Defy and ICL performing better.
"Tedelex lost some money...but Defy and ICL were better," an analyst said.
"Malbak motors was also not so bad," another said.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast group earnings in the year to August 31 of between 181.3 and 184.0 cents a share, with consensus at 182.1 cents, from 164.8 cents last year.
The dividend was put at between 50.6 and 51.4 cents, with consensus at 51.4, from 46.0 cents.
Results are due out on Monday.

Malbak said at the last financial year results that when the government's Reconstruction and Development Programme kicked in, earnings would be boosted. Analysts said the RDP was not in line with expectations but some subsidiaries had benefitted from it.
"The RDP was disappointing. Ellerine (Holdings Ltd ) said they had beneffited from the RDP. I suppose it is not as much as they would have wanted it," an analyst said.
Analysts are also on the look out for the company's unbundling plans.
Malbak said in August it would go ahead with a full unbundling of its assets and would make a further announcement when it published its preliminary results.
